title: EraseWork — witness-ledger deletion flow and tenant notification orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need a reliable, auditable deletion experience that ties a user-initiated right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) request to verifiable deletion outcomes across control plane and data plane assets, and surfaces clear notifications and downloadable receipts to tenants. Current gaps: deletion tasks are spread across multiple services (ingestion, S3, Redis, vector DBs, backups), there is no single canonical deletion ledger, and Console notifications for completed deletes are inconsistent. Goal: implement 'EraseWork' — an orchestrated deletion workflow that records witness-ledger entries for each logical delete, provides tenant-facing receipts, exposes an audit API, and wires tenant notification orchestration (Console + webhooks + email). This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the initial MVP (hosted + Dedicated) with private deployment considerations deferred to a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: When a tenant requests RTBF via Console or the Delete API, the system creates a single EraseWork job and returns a transaction id to caller
For each EraseWork job, the orchestration emits a witness-ledger record containing timestamp, scope (tenant, deletion selectors), list of target systems, and cryptographic hash of deletion manifest
All data-plane deletions (object storage, vector DBs, caches, backups) attempt to reach acknowledged delete states; transient failures are retried and recorded on the ledger with failure reasons
Tenant can view a downloadable deletion receipt in Console and via the new /audit/deletes/{job_id} API, containing the ledger entries and a verification hash
Notifications are sent to configured tenant endpoints (console notifications, email, webhook) on job start, partial failures, and successful completion
A monitoring dashboard surfaces per-tenant delete throughput, failure rate, average completion latency, and outstanding jobs; alerts fire when failures exceed threshold
Deletion runs are idempotent and safe to re-run; re-run events append to ledger rather than overwrite, preserving history
Security review signoff completed for KMS usage pattern and exposure of deletion metadata to tenant UI
implementation_notes: Define EraseWork job schema in control plane: job_id, tenant_id, selectors, created_at, state, target_systems, manifest_hash
Ledger will be append-only storage in the control plane backed by writable, signed records; initial implementation uses existing audit-db with an additional verifiable hash column

Data-plane adapters: implement delete adapters for S3, vector DB, Redis, Postgres, snapshot cleaner. Each adapter must return per-target status and optional proof token (e.g., deletion marker or tombstone hash)
Orchestrator will run state machine: CREATED -> IN_PROGRESS -> PARTIAL_FAILURE -> RETRYING -> COMPLETED -> FAILED and emit ledger updates at each transition
Expose API endpoints: POST /v1/deletes (create), GET /v1/deletes/{id} (status + ledger), GET /v1/deletes/{id}/receipt (downloadable JSON with ledger + hashes)
Tenant notifications: Console toast + page, webhook subscription support, and tenant email template. Add toggle to tenant settings for notification preferences
Ensure RBAC: delete job visibility scoped to tenant admins; support for org-admin elevated flows for enterprise customers
Plan for Private/VPC: ledger storage can be customer-managed in a future iteration; initial PRD assumes Redwood-managed ledger for hosted and Dedicated
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): implement orchestration, ledger entries, S3/Postgres/Redis adapters, Console UI for job creation and receipt download. Deploy to staging and internal beta tenants
Phase 2: add vector DB and backup purge adapters, webhook notifications, monitoring dashboard, and run load testing against orgs with large object counts
Phase 3: hardened retries, rate limiting, and private deployment compatibility (customer-managed ledger). Gradual ramp to 20% tenants, monitoring burn-in for 2 weeks before wider rollout
Communication: pre-release email to enterprise customers, docs in Confluence and developer docs for API consumers, update security/compliance pack
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: deletes.job.count by state, deletes.latency.p50/p95, deletes.failure.rate by tenant, deletes.outstanding.count
Alerts: page on deletes.failure.rate > 5% for >15m for top-tier tenants, warn on deletes.outstanding.count > 1000 across control plane, pager duty runbook link attached
SLO: 95% of single-tenant delete jobs complete within 72 hours for medium-sized tenants (<=10M tokens indexed), 99% of API requests to create a job should succeed (5xx rate <0.1%)
